reference: GNU coreutils logname from the isolated runner's system tool PATH, invoked by stock Bash. Metadata expectations are based on Bash type/help builtins and the stock loadable's documented help text; no expectation is derived from the candidate output.
coverage: GNU no-argument login-name output in the runner’s fixed passwd environment
Documented independence from LOGNAME and USER environment variables
GNU rejection of extra non-option operands compared with the loadable contract
Candidate Bash builtin availability and help metadata
Option checks cover aliases, end-of-options, option ordering and invalid/extra-operand statuses; banners use content/identity invariants.
exclusions: A non-default successful login identity requires a controlled disposable PTY/session and matching login record (or an independently reviewed libc mock); the runner exposes only its fixed synthetic runner account.
Invalid-option diagnostic wording is checked for presence, not identical prefixes. Help/version stdout remains a complete byte comparison.

cases.purpose: The runner supplies a fixed synthetic passwd entry for runner, and GNU logname resolves that login name in this fixture. Checks the normal no-argument output and status path.
The documented contract ignores LOGNAME and USER; spoofed values must not replace the runner login name exposed by the isolated fixture.
GNU rejects extra non-option operands with status 1 and a diagnostic.
Checks GNU's diagnostic and status for an unsupported option; the reference expectation is validated by GNU logname before candidate comparison.
Compare complete help/version output and status with GNU logname, including implementation branding differences; no output normalization.

Bash metadata must document the operand rejection and environment independence.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t logname) || exit 1
[[ $kind == builtin ]] || exit 1
doc=$(help logname) || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"Display user login name."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"ignores the LOGNAME and USER variables."* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *"rejects operands."* ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' builtin 'help text includes documented logname contract'
cases.stdout:
builtin
help text includes documented logname contract

cases.purpose: Verify that a non-default controlled login-session identity is returned, and that spoofed environment values do not replace it.
cases.reason: glibc getlogin() reads /proc/self/loginuid (2000, written by the guest controller for legacy runs, guest.py:390) and maps it through passwd. Inside a user namespace the loginuid is translated to the inner id, so mapping 2000 to an inner uid with its own bind-mounted passwd row yields a non-default login name without privilege.
